pages.description: The Wikipedia articles linked from the text, in the order they appear in it. Related reading, not the article about the event; may be empty.

year.description: The year. Negative before the common era.

width.description: Width in pixels. Originals can be very large: check before loading one.

countryCount.description: In how many countries those events are.

indexedAt.description: When the newest of these events was written to the index: how far behind Wikipedia it can be.

newestYear.description: The newest year of any indexed event.

oldestYear.description: The oldest year of any indexed event. Negative before the common era.

after.description: "Dopo": what followed. Developments, not all direct effects: the text says which is which.

inPaths.description: The guided paths that have a stop on this insight, with its position: the way back to a path.

provenance.description: Who wrote it and when it was last really reviewed.

related.description: "Collegamenti": two or three insights worth reading next. Use them for "Continua a esplorare".

sources.description: Where each claim can be checked. Show them on the card, not only on a general page.

summary.description: The event in one or two sentences.

message.description: The limit, in Italian, to show as it is.

stopCount.description: How many stops the path has.

date.description: The day that was asked for.

language.description: The language that was asked for. Each section says which one it really came from.

sections.description: The sections asked for, keyed by name: selected, events, births, deaths, holidays. Always in that order.

warnings.description: Things worth telling the user about how this answer was put together. PRIMARY_UNAVAILABLE: the language asked for could not be fetched and every section comes from the fallback. FALLBACK_UNAVAILABLE: a gap in the language asked for could not be filled.

PageRef.description: A Wikipedia article linked from an item's text. Related reading, not the article about the event: its description and extract describe the article, not what happened.

coordinates.description: Where the article's subject is. Absent for most pages: only places have one.

description.description: Wikipedia's one-line description of the article. Absent when it has none.

extract.description: The opening paragraph of the article, as plain text. Absent when it has none.

originalImage.description: The same picture at full size, for a detail view. Absent when there is no thumbnail.

thumbnail.description: A small picture for lists. Absent when the article has none from Commons.

url.description: The article on Wikipedia. Link to it whenever you show its text: the licence requires it.

wikibaseItem.description: The Wikidata id, the same in every language: match a page across it and en with it.

cover.description: The cover image. Absent when the path has none.

endYear.description: The year of the path's latest stop. Negative before the common era.

intro.description: A short introduction: where the path starts and what it follows.

language.description: The language of every text here. Editorial content is written in Italian only.

readingMinutes.description: Estimated minutes to read the whole path, counted from its words.

startYear.description: The year of the path's earliest stop. Negative before the common era.

stops.description: The stops, in order. Open the first, then step to the previous or the next by position.

tagline.description: One sentence on what the path is about.

topic.description: What the path is about, from a closed list.

topicLabel.description: The topic's name to show, in Italian.

cover.description: The cover image. Absent when the path has none: the card has to work without it.

endYear.description: The year of the path's latest stop. Negative before the common era.

startYear.description: The year of the path's earliest stop, read from the stops' dates. Negative before the common era.

stopCount.description: How many stops the path has.

topic.description: What the path is about, from a closed list. Paths are listed grouped by it, in the order the topics are declared.

year.description: The year; negative before the common era.

reason.description: Why it is worth reading next. A reason to read, not a claim of cause.

id.description: The report's number. Quote it if the visitor writes back about it.

contact.description: An email address to answer at. Optional, and only used to reply about this report.

message.description: What is wrong, in the visitor's words: 10 to 1000 characters.

eventCount.description: How many events of the window are in the index, after leaving out the excluded country.

note.description: What the index leaves out, in Italian. Show it, whatever the level: even OK is a selection.

comparison.description: What these events are: TEMPORAL, always. They were contemporary; nothing says one led to another.

countries.description: The countries with events in the window, most events first. Each lists the ones closest to the year, oldest first.

coverage.description: How much the index has for this window, and what it leaves out. Show the note.

excludedCountry.description: The country left out, as asked. Absent when none was.

fromYear.description: First year of the window, inclusive.

notice.description: A sentence to show with the events, in Italian: they are a comparison in time, not causes and effects.

toYear.description: Last year of the window, inclusive.

SectionResult.description: One section of the day, and where it really came from.

fallback.description: True when the language asked for had nothing for this section and another one was used. The Italian feed has no births or deaths, so those arrive in English. Say so rather than present English text as Italian.

language.description: The edition that supplied these items. It is not always the one asked for.

stale.description: True when this is a copy older than six hours because Wikipedia could not be reached to refresh it. Old history is served in preference to an error.

license.description: The licence of the text, when it has one that asks for a credit.

title.description: What the link is, as it should be shown.

index.description: The country index, per Wikipedia edition: how many events, how many countries, which years, how recent. Empty until its first pass has run.

SourcesResponse.description: Where the content comes from, under what terms, how much there is and what it leaves out.

coverage.description: How much content there is, as it stands now.

limits.description: What the content is not, in Italian. Show it on the project page, in full.

sources.description: The sources of everything the service shows, with the terms of each.

teaser.description: Why to begin here, in a sentence.

narrative.description: Why the path comes here, from the stop before: the thread that makes the stops a story.

place.description: Where the map should go. Check `approximate`.

position.description: Its place in the path, counting from 1.

slug.description: The insight this stop opens: ask for it at /api/history/insights/{slug} to show the stop's content.

summary.description: The event in one or two sentences.

Target.description: What a report is about. An EVENT is named by its date and edition; an INSIGHT or a PATH by its slug.

day.description: For an EVENT: the day of the month.

language.description: For an EVENT: the edition it was read in, it or en. Defaults to it.

month.description: For an EVENT: the month of the day page it is listed on, 1 to 12.

slug.description: For an INSIGHT or a PATH: its slug. Not for an EVENT.

text.description: For an EVENT: its text as the visitor saw it; anything past 500 characters is cut. It helps find the entry again, since an event has no identifier.

year.description: For an EVENT: its year. Negative before the common era.

Every event with a year that Wikipedia lists on any day of the year and that the map's
own rule places in this country: the first linked article with coordinates, inside the
country's Natural Earth 1:110m shape. Rebuilt every night, so up to a day behind
Wikipedia. A valid code with nothing indexed is an empty list, not an error.

get.description:
Without parameters, every insight, oldest first. With `month` and `day`, only those of
that day of the year, whatever the year: the way to know which of a day's events from
/api/history/on-this-day to mark "Approfondimento disponibile". Match them on `date.year`.
An insight whose `date.precision` is not `DAY` (only the year, or the month, is known)
belongs to no day and is left out. A day with none is an empty list, not an error.

get.description:
What led up to the event (`before`), what happened (`event`) and what followed
(`after`), plus two or three insights to read next (`related`), the paths it belongs
to, its sources, caveats about dates and places, and who wrote it. Written in Italian.

get.description:
Selected entries, events, births, deaths and holidays for one day of the year, from
Wikipedia. Each section says which language it really came from: the Italian feed has
no births or deaths, so those arrive in English with `fallback: true`.

In every item, `text` is the event and `pages` are the articles linked from it, in
the order they appear - related reading, not the article about the event.

The year filter narrows one day; Wikipedia cannot answer "everything in 1789".

parameters.description: Month, 1 to 12.
parameters.name: month

parameters.description: Day of the month. It has to exist in that month: 2/29 is valid, 2/30 is a 400.
parameters.name: day

parameters.description: Language of the text.
parameters.name: lang

parameters.description: Which sections to return, comma-separated or repeated. All five when omitted.
parameters.name: types

parameters.description: Only items from this year, such as `1969`. Negative before the common era (`-44`). Cannot be combined with fromYear or toYear; holidays have no year and are left out.
parameters.name: year

parameters.description: Only items from this year on, inclusive, such as `1900`.
parameters.name: fromYear

parameters.description: Only items up to this year, inclusive, such as `1999`.
parameters.name: toYear

200.description: The day, in the usual envelope. Cached for five minutes (thirty seconds when the answer is degraded: a stale copy, or a language that could not be reached).

400.description: The request cannot be answered and Wikipedia was not asked. `error` is one of INVALID_DATE, UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE, INVALID_TYPE, INVALID_YEAR, BAD_REQUEST.

502.description: Wikipedia answered with something unusable, for instance because its API changed. `error` is UPSTREAM_BAD_RESPONSE.

503.description: Wikipedia could not be used and there was no copy or other language to fall back on. `error` is UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE, or UPSTREAM_RATE_LIMITED with a `Retry-After` header saying for how long.

line that ties it to the path. A stop's full explanation is the insight with the stop's
slug, asked for when the stop is opened.

get.description:
One event picked at random from the country index, from those that match the filters
the visitor has active: a country, and a range of years. Every call can answer
differently, so it is never cached. The event carries its date and country: open the day
with /api/history/on-this-day/{month}/{day} for its articles and images.

Only events with a year that the map can place in a country are in the index, about
half of what Wikipedia lists. When nothing matches the filters the answer is a 200 with
no `event`.

parameters.description: Language of the text.
parameters.name: lang

post.description:
The frontend fills in `target` from the card the visitor is on, so the visitor only says
what is wrong. An EVENT is named by its date and edition (it has no identifier of its
own); an INSIGHT or a PATH by its slug. Nothing identifying the visitor is stored; the
email address is optional and only for replying.

Limited per visitor and for the whole service: a 429 carries `Retry-After`.

201.description: The report was stored. Its number is in the answer.

400.description: The report cannot be stored. `error` is INVALID_REPORT, INVALID_DATE, INVALID_YEAR, UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE or BAD_REQUEST (no body, a body that is not this shape, or one over 8 KB).

429.description: Too many reports. `error` is TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, with `Retry-After`.

post.summary: Report a mistake in an event, an insight or a path

get.description:
What the country index has for the years around `year`, grouped by country, leaving out
`excludeCountry` - normally the one the visitor is looking at. A comparison in time and
nothing more: the events were contemporary, not connected, and the answer says so in
`notice`.

The index is a selection (what Wikipedia lists on its day pages and the map can place),
so `coverage` says how much there is for the window: NONE, SPARSE or OK. Show its note
and do not draw conclusions from a SPARSE window.

parameters.description: The year at the centre of the window. Negative before the common era.
parameters.name: year

parameters.description: Years either side of `year`, 0 to 25.
parameters.name: span

parameters.description: Language of the texts.
parameters.name: lang

parameters.description: Leave out this country, usually the one being looked at. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, uppercase.
parameters.name: excludeCountry

parameters.description: How many events of each country to show, 1 to 10.
parameters.name: perCountry

200.description: The countries with events in the window, most events first. A window with nothing in it is a 200 with `coverage.level` NONE. Cached for five minutes.

400.description: `error` is INVALID_YEAR, INVALID_SPAN, INVALID_LIMIT, INVALID_COUNTRY_CODE, UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE or BAD_REQUEST (a value that is not a number, or no `year`).

get.description:
For the project and sources page: every source of content with its licence and whether it
must be credited, how much content there is (the country index per edition, and how many
paths and insights, of which how many were reviewed), and what the content is not.

It is provenance, not a seal of reliability: nothing in it says "verified". An insight
with a review date was checked by a person; every other text is Wikipedia's, shown with
where it comes from.

200.description: The sources. Cached for five minutes.
